status.en: 62 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 38% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Peshawar.
status.nb: 62 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 38 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Peshawar.

summary.en: Security forces killed eight terrorists in operations in Peshawar and Bannu, while a former soldier was killed by armed men in Kabul. A building collapse in Karachi injured many and killed at least one person, and residents of Bajaur district died in a shipwreck off Libya. Afghanistan sentenced five nationals to prison for illegal border crossing and a Kabul shootout left six suspected robbers dead, while fresh fruit exports fell sharply after Pakistan closed its border. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker drepte åtte terrorister i operasjoner i Peshawar og Bannu, mens en tidligere soldat ble drept av bevæpnede menn i Kabul. Et bygg sammenfalt i Karachi, mange ble såret og minst én person døde, og innbyggere i Bajaur-distriktet omkom i en skipsforlis utenfor Libya. Afghanistan dømte fem nasjonale til fengsel for ulovlig grensekryssing, og en skyteepisode i Kabul etterlot seks mistenkte røvere døde, mens eksporten av fersk frukt falt kraftig etter at Pakistan stengte grensen. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
